description:
FILED s461ar (agent AR, round 18).  The census is 17 files / 57 drops and the
CLASSIFICATION of every one of them is now written down, so no future session
has to re-derive it:

    39  t/op/sub_lval.t x33 + substr.t x2 + t/op/substr.t x2 + signatures.t +
        try.t  -- user `:lvalue` subs.  BLESSED non-support, sized with a
        measured 8-shape table in task #930.  Do not revisit.
     4  perl-tests/method.t, perl-tests/ref.t, t/op/method.t, t/op/ref.t --
        the SCALAR-INVOCANT indirect object (`new $obj "a"`).  USER: MAYBE
        LATER (s425).  `new Foo` and `new Foo(LIST)` already work.
     2  board/Mojo-DOM58 _Collection.pm -- `local (*{"${caller}::a"})`, task
        #564; the `local` fall-through loses it SILENTLY, so trading a loud
        drop for a silent one is the wrong direction.
     7  DELIBERATE parser torture, i.e. rows that ASSERT perl rejects the
        source (CLAUDE.md principle 9): t/comp/final_line_num.t's `print 1+`,
        t/comp/parser.t x5, and -- newly classified here -- t/op/write.t:1930,
        `ok !eval q| format = @<<< } ;1 |, 'format = ... } is not allowed'`.
     1  perl-tests/sprintf2.t -- a PPI structure bug, task #937.
     1  t/re/pat.t -- FIXED s461ar, task #931.  (Row already removed.)
     3  the three below, each diagnosed and none of them bounded today.

1. t/op/filetest.t:161 `sub _ { "this is not a file name" }`
   PPI lexes `_` after the `sub` keyword as a Token::Magic (the stat handle),
   so it never builds a Statement::Sub and the statement swallows the next one.
   Probed: `_` is the ONLY name PPI gets wrong there -- `sub y`, `sub s`,
   `sub q`, `sub m`, `sub tr`, `sub qq`, `sub x`, `sub lc`, `sub if` all lex as
   Statement::Sub with a Word.  perl gives all four answers the file wants
   (`-f _` is the stat handle BEFORE and AFTER the definition; `_()` and
   `&_()` call the sub).
   WHY THE ORDINARY REPAIR SHAPE DOES NOT WORK: every `_repair_*` in
   Pl/Parser2.pm ends in `_reparse_doc`, which SERIALIZES the document and
   re-parses the TEXT -- so re-blessing the token to a Word does not survive,
   and there is no text change that renames `_` while keeping it `_`.  The two
   ways out are (a) reparse under a placeholder name and then rename the
   Statement::Sub's name TOKEN in the tree (no second reparse), or (b) an
   in-place structural repair like `_merge_unicode_symbols` (#410), which
   already re-classes tokens after the lexer has built the wrong shape.
   Cost of the drop: the file is C 184/250; the swallow takes ONE assertion.

2. t/op/lex.t:99 `is ${no strict; \$_}, "rhubarb", '${no strict; ...}';`
   A deref BLOCK containing STATEMENTS: PPI gives Statement::Include +
   Statement inside the braces and the expression walker has a case for one
   expression only.  Same family as task #463 item 5 (`${;EXPR}`), one step
   further: the block's value is its LAST statement, and the pragma before it
   has to be honoured as a compile-time hint.  A feature, not a repair.

3. t/op/lexsub.t:851 `is y, 43, 'my sub that looks like constant closure';`
   `y` is a LEXICAL sub declared above (`my sub y`), and PPI lexes
   `y, 43, '...';` as a Token::Regexp::Transliterate, swallowing the rest of
   the file's block.  This IS the `_repair_word_x_call` / `_repair_word_match`
   family -- the condition is the same negative, `_document_declares_sub('y')`
   -- but the repair has to rewrite the mis-lexed token's CONTENT (`y` ->
   `y()` plus the swallowed tail) rather than a one-character operator, so it
   is a bigger and riskier edit than its siblings.  `s`, `m`, `tr`, `q`, `qq`
   are the same shape and should be settled together.
subject: the drop census SINGLES, diagnosed one by one (s461ar harvest): sub _, ${no strict; ...}, `is y, 43`, and one more deliberate row
